verdict: JPMorgan earned $15.3B in the quarter as net interest income jumped 13% — and it would have been $15.8B without $658M of investment securities losses booked in Corporate.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: reported basis, vs a year ago

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus the interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, up 13% as loan and deposit balances grew.

segments.name: Noninterest revenue
segments.note: Fees, trading and asset-management income — up only 3%, held back by $658M of investment securities losses. Asset management fees rose 15% and Markets revenue 15%.

opex.name: Compensation expense
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's workforce — its biggest cost, up 9% on hiring and revenue-related pay.

opex.name: Professional & outside services
opex.note: Outside services and professional fees — up 23%.

opex.name: Technology, communications & equipment
opex.note: Technology, telecoms and equipment — up 17% as the bank invests in AI and its platforms.

opex.name: Occupancy & other expense
opex.note: Branches and offices ($1,525M of occupancy) plus other general costs ($1,849M).

takeaways.title: Interest income is the engine
takeaways.text: Net interest income rose 13% to $27.0B on bigger loan and deposit balances — average loans up 10% YoY. It is now 54% of all revenue.

takeaways.title: One item hides the strength
takeaways.text: Excluding $658M of investment securities losses in Corporate, net income was $15.8B and EPS $5.75 instead of $5.57 — a return on tangible equity of 21% rather than 20%.

takeaways.title: Credit costs are contained
takeaways.text: The bank set aside $2.7B for credit losses — $2.2B of actual charge-offs plus a $539M reserve build — down from $3.4B a year ago, even as lending grew.

follow100Note: JPMorgan reports revenue two ways: $50.2B reported (GAAP), used here, or $50.9B on a 'managed' basis that grosses up tax-exempt income. Net income is identical either way.
oneTimers: $658M of net investment securities losses in Corporate — the quarter's flagged 'significant item'. Excluding it, net income was $15.8B ($5.75 per share) instead of $15.3B ($5.57).
footerNote: JPMorgan headlines 'managed' revenue of $50.9B; this page uses reported (GAAP) revenue of $50.2B — the difference is a tax gross-up that does not change net income. For a bank, credit costs (the provision for credit losses) play the role of cost of revenue.
